title: Shanahan Talks Defensive Growth, Praises WR Mike Evans' Impact
headline: Jordan Watkins and Malik Mustapha are gaining real opportunity while Deebo Samuel is trending toward IR, and McCaffrey's touches are being deliberately managed.
summary: Shanahan opened with injury news: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is out and could be placed on IR, with the bye week as the main hope to avoid that move; Garret Wallow (hamstring) and Nick Bosa (calf) are out, and Upton Stout (shoulder) and Colton McKivitz (illness) are limited. DeMarcus Robinson remains on IR, with a long-shot chance at returning around the bye. He praised Jordan Watkins for earning respect through more targets and blocking while others were hurt, and said Malik Mustapha was one of the game's MVPs after getting every rep with Marques Sigle out. On Christian McCaffrey, he said the team is deliberately rotating him to keep him fresh, though early-season game flow pushed usage up more than planned. He framed the Commanders as a hungry, dangerous team coming off a tough loss, and called this week potentially his team's biggest challenge yet. On defense, he credited Raheem Morris's background and the secondary's experience and communication for the growth of the DBs, who have to play more aggressively without linebacker help. He spoke glowingly about Brock Purdy and Mike Evans, who have connected faster than expected, and said Evans will get the ball with the QB just waiting for him to come down with it. Note: the transcript has several garbled names and includes references to Atlanta and Jayden Daniels that don't clearly match the Commanders framing in the title, so some attributions are uncertain.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/16/26
headline: Trey Amos and Nick Cross are back to full practice, Austin Ekeler is back in the backfield, and Leo Chenal is out for the year; Stefon Diggs and Percy Butler sat today but may return this week.
summary: Quinn opened by saying the team has moved past a tough Sunday loss that ended in overtime and is focused on Monday night's game against San Francisco. He said Trey Amos and Nick Cross were worked back into practice last week and should have full loads, and that a running back named Jay Mack (name garbled in the transcript) is also back. He took responsibility for the late-game breakdowns, said the defense's late-game lapses came down to failing to respond in key moments, and praised Terry McLaurin's performance. Quinn said Stefon Diggs, Percy Butler and Leo Chenal did not practice, that he hopes Diggs and Butler get reps later in the week, and that Chenal is out for the year after an injury. He described work on penalties, including pre-snap cadence discipline and more officials at practice, and said he would make some game-management adjustments. On the running backs, he said Ekeler's return adds a pass-game element, and that the group has been strong in pass protection. Quinn also said the offense will need answers ready for more blitzes, and that the matchup with San Francisco will come down to clean, disciplined play.

The team is working on pre-snap cadence discipline, using more officials at practice, and planning game-management adjustments.
Quinn said the team is working on end-of-half situations and wants to eliminate one-off mistakes that waste time or chances.
Quinn said the offense needs answers ready against more blitzes, with man coverage and back-turned matchups as possible advantages.
San Francisco is 5-0 with balanced defense and strong early-down run game, and Quinn expects a physical game where avoiding self-inflicted mistakes decides the outcome.
